title: Bupropion interaction model: clinical discrepancy and metabolite sensitivity
classification: retrospective literature reconstruction; not prospective or participant-matched validation
scope: A static CYP2D6 comparison at published steady-state inhibitor concentrations. Study-case calculations do not create metabolites in the interactive bloodstream simulation.
concentrationSource: Tanaudommongkon et al. (2025), Table 1; steady-state Cmax values attributed there to Kharasch et al. (2020). Unbound concentrations combine those total plasma measurements with separately measured in-vitro plasma binding.
concentrationContext: Adults receiving chronic oral bupropion XL 300 mg/day in the concentration-source study. These are not measured inhibitor concentrations in each interaction-study participant, simultaneous within-person mixture maxima, or a single virtual injection.

componentEvidence.potency: Competitive inhibition of dextromethorphan O-demethylation in pooled human liver microsomes. Apparent Ki; authors found microsomal unbound fractions close to one.
componentEvidence.units: Table 1 micromolar values multiplied by 1000 to store nM. Published unbound concentrations are stored directly to avoid compounding rounded total concentration and rounded free-fraction errors.
componentEvidence.bindingConflict: This experiment's approximately 70% unbound parent fraction differs from the catalog's 16% unbound label-based value. Neither is silently replaced; the benchmark supplies study-context unbound concentrations directly.

liverScale.provenance: Tanaudommongkon et al. (2025) adopts a ratio based on rat quantitative whole-body autoradiography after carbon-14-labeled hydroxybupropion, attributed to Reese et al. (2008).
liverScale.limitations: Neither bound is a measured human unbound liver concentration or a confidence interval. Applying one scale to all parent/metabolite pools and from single animal exposure to chronic human exposure is an assumption. The mean of endpoint predictions is a descriptive midpoint, not a fitted optimum.

cases.label: Desipramine
cases.fractionProvenance: Literature value used in the 2025 paper, attributed to Reese et al. (2008); not derived here from the observed 5.2 ratio.
cases.observedEndpoint: Parent desipramine plasma AUC with versus without bupropion
cases.regimen: Open-label two-period study: desipramine 50 mg on day 1 and day 22; bupropion 150 mg/day on days 8–10, 300 mg/day on days 11–21, and 150 mg with the day-22 probe.

cases.label: Nebivolol
cases.fractionProvenance: Estimated from a separate pharmacogenetic study (Briciu et al., 2014), as reported in the 2025 analysis; not estimated from this bupropion interaction endpoint.
cases.observedEndpoint: Parent nebivolol plasma AUC with versus without bupropion
cases.regimen: Open-label two-period study: nebivolol 5 mg on day 1 and day 8; bupropion pretreatment 150 mg/day for 3 days then 300 mg/day for 4 days, with 300 mg on the probe day.

cases.label: Atomoxetine
cases.fractionProvenance: Estimated from pharmacogenetic data (Brown et al., 2016), as reported in the 2025 analysis; not estimated from this bupropion interaction endpoint.
cases.observedEndpoint: Parent atomoxetine plasma AUC with versus without bupropion
cases.regimen: Open-label two-period study: atomoxetine 25 mg alone and after 7 days of bupropion pretreatment (150 mg/day for 3 days then 300 mg/day for 4 days), with 300 mg bupropion on the probe day.

cases.label: Dextromethorphan
cases.fractionProvenance: Literature value attributed to Nakashima et al. (2007) in the 2025 analysis; not estimated from this bupropion interaction endpoint.
cases.observedEndpoint: Dextromethorphan plasma AUC with versus without bupropion
cases.population: Healthy volunteers; clinical result attributed to Duong et al. (2020) by the 2025 paper
cases.regimen: Open-label two-period study: dextromethorphan 30 mg on days 1 and 22; bupropion 150 mg/day for 3 days then 150 mg twice daily for 16 days, with 150 mg on the probe day.
cases.retrievalLimit: Clinical endpoint and protocol were verified in the 2025 paper's Table 2; the Duong clinical report was not independently retrieved.

cases.label: Vortioxetine
cases.fractionProvenance: Estimated from pharmacogenetic data (Frederiksen et al., 2022), as reported in the 2025 analysis; not estimated from this bupropion interaction endpoint.
cases.observedEndpoint: Steady-state vortioxetine plasma AUC with versus without bupropion
cases.regimen: Vortioxetine 10 mg/day on days 1–28; compare day 14 with day 28 after bupropion 75 mg twice daily for 3 days then 150 mg twice daily on days 18–28.

limitations: This is a retrospective reconstruction of an existing literature analysis, not a new blinded holdout or proof of clinical predictive validity.
Shared Cmax inputs come from another cohort and formulation; they do not recreate participant-level inhibitor exposure in each interaction trial.
Fraction metabolized values are literature estimates, not individual measurements; genotype, hepatic distribution and bioavailability may vary.
Static peak concentrations omit absorption, metabolite formation and elimination, delayed onset and washout, and enzyme adaptation.
The liver range is a sensitivity interval from animal-derived assumptions, not statistical uncertainty or a prediction interval.
No clinical effect, safety, neuronal firing, or cognitive endpoint is tested by a plasma AUC comparison.
These reference substrate cases do not add those drugs to the live catalog or apply their AUC ratios to another compound.
